scope: Undergraduate-to-graduate discovery for eight modeled AUI undergraduate programs. Seven existing graduate planners plus separately identified exploration-only AUI targets. Global topics are search starting points with verified official examples.

instructions: Match selected interests to tags and explain the matched subjects in a sentence.
Use the student’s chosen degree to distinguish documented preparation from broader thematic exploration.
Let the student compare and choose; do not assign invented percentages or claim admission eligibility.
Selecting a graduate target never automatically removes undergraduate credits, counts shared courses, adds foundations or changes course codes.
AUI is the source for academic facts; interest mappings are GoPlan’s stated inference from those facts.
No global example implies partnership, scholarship, admission, exchange status or current open applications.

policies.title: General AUI graduate admission
policies.text: A recognized bachelor’s degree or equivalent, adequate preparation and evidence of graduate-study ability are required. A B average in upper-level work is one stated route; other evidence may be considered. The general recommendation for CGPA 3.0 is not a universal automatic cutoff. Program-specific requirements take precedence. GRE/GMAT are encouraged, not generally mandatory.

policies.title: SSE admission and foundations
policies.text: For AUI BSc applicants, the catalog states as a rule CGPA at least 2.50 and major-area GPA at least 3.00, with transcript, two faculty recommendations and possible interview. Other applicants normally need GPA 3.00 or at least two Assez Bien distinctions/equivalent and may face an interview and placement exam. Program-specific subject requirements still apply. Up to 24 foundation credits may be assigned.

policies.title: Documented SSE breadth preparation
policies.text: The catalog identifies BSCSC as satisfying MSSE breadth; BSCSC with AI or Big Data Analytics specialization for MSBDA breadth; and BSEMS, BSGE or BSRESE for MSSEM breadth. This is preparation evidence, not admission, a universal prerequisite waiver or an accelerated-route approval. Graduate course prerequisites must still be satisfied.

policies.title: SSE culminating registration
policies.text: General SSE policy permits project/thesis registration after at least four courses in the specific program. Program-specific MSSE, MSSEM and MSBDA requirements prescribe 6 credits over two consecutive semesters, with no more than 3 of those credits in Summer and the other 3 in Fall or Spring. The general statement that a project normally takes one semester conflicts with these more specific provisions. Registration codes have inconsistencies and require coordinator confirmation.

policies.title: SSAH research preparation
policies.text: Normally a 6-credit SSAH Research Academy is required before degree courses. AUI graduates entering another field may instead need the 3-credit version; AUI graduates continuing in the same field are normally exempt unless away from university at least five years. The admissions committee can require it after individual assessment. These foundation credits are outside the master’s degree total.

policies.title: Graduate English requirements vary by program
policies.text: The general policy uses TOEFL 550/equivalent for regular study and 450/equivalent for Language Center entry. MACDM/MAISD program provisions instead specify 500–549 for their Language Center route, plus detailed writing/iBT equivalents. Do not calculate admission using a single university-wide English threshold.

auiMasters.name: Master of Science in Software Engineering
auiMasters.admissionSummary: Bachelor’s in computer science or a closely related discipline; standard SSE admission and foundation requirements apply.
notes: 24 coursework credits + 6 thesis/project credits.
Cloud and Edge Computing is CSC 5373 in the degree table but CSC 5374 in the course description and supplied sheet.

auiMasters.name: Master of Science in Big Data Analytics
auiMasters.admissionSummary: Engineering graduates; bachelor’s in CS, data science or related disciplines; mathematics with a CS minor; or BA graduates with a CS minor. The catalog’s wording “BA graduates” should be confirmed for an individual BBA or other degree.
notes: 18 core + 6 approved elective + 6 thesis/project credits.
A CS minor alone does not establish every course prerequisite or admission eligibility.

auiMasters.name: Master of Science in Sustainable Energy Management
auiMasters.admissionSummary: Bachelor’s in engineering; formal selection considers English, GPA, capstone and possible experience/interview. Up to 24 foundation credits may be assigned.
notes: 24 coursework + 6 thesis/project credits.
Environmental Studies and Sustainability is not automatically treated as an engineering bachelor for admission.

auiMasters.name: Master of Business Administration
auiMasters.admissionSummary: Bachelor’s/equivalent with minimum B standing; complete application and interview. Non-business entrants or students missing prerequisites may need foundation courses.
notes: Concentrations depend on enrollment and market opportunities; they are not guaranteed every semester.
Choose a coherent concentration and a thesis, coursework or internship route. The internship is at least six months full time after coursework.
Up to 12 foundation credits may be additional to the degree.

auiMasters.name: Master of Science in Digital Marketing and Analytics
auiMasters.admissionSummary: Bachelor’s/equivalent with minimum B standing, some professional experience, interview, application and applicable English evidence. GMAT is highly recommended.
notes: Eight core courses and two electives: 30 degree credits. Up to 12 business foundation credits may be additional.
The exit section says minimum B in every course; the structure section says repeat below B−. Confirm the governing threshold.

auiMasters.name: Master of Arts in Communication and Digital Media
auiMasters.admissionSummary: Formal selection and possible oral interview; AUI candidates need CGPA at least 3.00. Program English, writing and possible SSAHRA preparation requirements apply.
notes: 15 required + 15 optional credits, with thesis seminar or applied practicum.
Thesis II immediately follows Thesis I in Summer; thesis courses must be completed at AUI. The practicum route has separate last-semester/final-project wording.

auiMasters.name: Master of Arts in International Studies and Diplomacy
auiMasters.admissionSummary: Formal selection and possible oral interview; AUI candidates need CGPA at least 3.00. Program English, writing and possible SSAHRA preparation requirements apply.
notes: Standalone degree: 18 core + 12 optional credits.
The combined BAIS route instead lists 15 core + 15 optional graduate credits; do not silently substitute the standalone curriculum.

auiMasters.name: Master of Science in Cybersecurity
auiMasters.admissionSummary: Bachelor’s in computer science or equivalent, with a solid cybersecurity foundation. The catalog identifies BSCSC Cybersecurity specialization as one way to develop that foundation.
notes: Exploration target: a full verified semester roadmap has not been implemented.
30 credits comprise 21 core, 3 special topics and 6 project/thesis. No approved combined BSCSC/MSCSEC pairing is listed on p348.

auiMasters.name: Master of Arts in North African and Middle Eastern Studies
auiMasters.admissionSummary: BA degree with GPA 3.0 or equivalent; program-specific English and SSAHRA conditions apply. The program welcomes several social-science and humanities backgrounds.
notes: Exploration target; 18 required + 12 optional degree credits.
BAIS–NAMES combined route is described separately on p344.

auiMasters.name: Master of Science in Governance, Development and Public Policy
auiMasters.admissionSummary: Formal selection and possible oral interview; AUI candidates need CGPA at least 3.00. Program-specific English and SSAHRA requirements apply.
notes: Exploration target; 22 required + 9 optional credits and a field-based final project.

auiMasters.name: Master of Science in Human Resource Development
auiMasters.admissionSummary: Formal selection and possible oral interview; AUI candidates need CGPA at least 3.00. Program-specific English and SSAHRA requirements apply.
notes: Exploration target; 24 required + 6 optional credits, including thesis research methods and thesis seminar.

auiMasters.name: Master of Science in Financial Technology
auiMasters.admissionSummary: Listed among SSE graduate programs. A complete program-specific admissions and curriculum description was not verified in this extraction; ask AUI about current intake and requirements.
notes: Listing-only exploration target. Do not create an automatic course plan or eligibility claim from this listing.

combinedRoutes.name: Combined BSCSC–MSSE
constraints: Select an approved combination and obtain admission.
Direct Fast-Track entry may apply with Mention Bien/equivalent and fewer than 48 accumulated credits.

In-study applicants need 48–129 completed credits, including at least 9 in the relevant major area (or 6 in each if more than one), CGPA ≥2.5, major-area GPA ≥3.0, faculty recommendations and available space.
Maintain CGPA ≥2.5 and at least B− in all undergraduate and graduate courses in the major area.
The approved combined plan waives the undergraduate capstone and up to 6 free-elective credits; apply waivers only after the individual route is confirmed.
Graduate requirements, foundations and prerequisites still apply.

combinedRoutes.name: Combined BSCSC–MSBDA
constraints: BSCSC specialization must be Artificial Intelligence or Big Data Analytics.
BSCCBDA–MSBDA is also listed but BSCCBDA is not one of the eight currently modeled undergraduate programs.

combinedRoutes.name: Combined engineering bachelor–MSSEM
constraints: The approved-pairing text covers engineering or engineering-and-management bachelors.
The specific Fast-Track structure covers BSEMS, BSGE and BSRESE and counts 12 MSSEM credits toward undergraduate thematic requirements and the graduate degree.
BSGE must also take EGR 3392 for the remaining thematic credits; BSRESE uses EGR 3392 as a free elective.
Specific Fast-Track retention: CGPA ≥2.5, major CGPA ≥3.0 and at least B− in graduate coursework.
The p349 specific route invokes requirements 1, 3 and 4 of p348, not its generic requirement 2. Do not automatically combine 12-credit sharing with the generic capstone/free-elective waiver.

combinedRoutes.name: Combined BAIS–MAISD
constraints: At least 60 completed credits and CGPA ≥3.00, plus declaration of intent/admission.
Maintain CGPA ≥3.00; one probation semester is described before removal for a continued shortfall.

Approved students retain the undergraduate internship, complete graduate thesis/policy work, and are exempt from the undergraduate senior capstone. SSAHRA/foundation wording differs between pp342–343.
The combined graduate table uses 15 required + 15 optional credits, unlike the standalone MAISD table.
Catalog p342 says 148 combined credits; p164 says 150. Obtain the governing combined plan before fixing a total or waivers.

combinedRoutes.name: Combined BAIS–NAMES
constraints: At least 60 completed credits, CGPA ≥3.00 and declaration/admission.
Maintain CGPA ≥3.00; one probation semester is described before removal for a continued shortfall.
Catalog states 148 combined credits, capstone exemption, retained undergraduate internship and graduate thesis.
Complete the applicable foundations during BAIS; this route is an exploration target, with no automated combined roadmap.

combinedRoutes.name: Accelerated Bachelor–MBA
constraints: Declare Accelerated Bachelor/MBA and use the required course-registration form signed by the SBA Graduate Programs Director.
Meet prerequisites and remain in good standing; individual pathway and foundation review is required.
Up to 9 MBA credits may count as undergraduate electives depending on the undergraduate program; at most 12 MBA core credits may be taken while in undergraduate status.
The operative course/residency rule on p313 specifies eligible MBA core courses, despite broader introductory language on p312.
MBA courses under this route must be taken at AUI, not on exchange.
After transition to MBA status, complete at least one year / 24 credits as an MBA student on campus.
Minimum B− (80%) for MBA credit and C (70%) for undergraduate elective credit.
Undergraduate elective registrations use XXX 3398 coding and formal later MBA equivalency; do not substitute a normal graduate-code elective without approval.
Additional graduate-coded credits have different aid/registration conditions.

auditCorrections.problem: Requiring every core course before first thesis/project registration is unsupported and can unnecessarily delay the plan.
auditCorrections.correction: Use the catalog p347 minimum of four successfully completed courses in that specific program, together with individual prerequisites/permission; retain the program-specific two-consecutive-semester requirement.

auditCorrections.problem: A choice with an empty options array currently accepts almost any known catalog course. An undergraduate minor/free-elective slot can thereby accept a graduate course without its formal route or satisfy a constrained requirement with an unrelated course.
auditCorrections.correction: Enforce category, level, minor membership and approved-route constraints. Separate an unverified proposed substitution from a valid resolved requirement. Keep unresolved status until approval is recorded for a non-listed choice.

auditCorrections.problem: The reviewed rule checks a programming alternative but drops the statistics alternative from the source prerequisite.
auditCorrections.correction: Represent (CSC1402 OR CSC1401 OR BAI3301) AND (EGR3393 OR GBU2301); retain review for individual program equivalencies.

auditCorrections.problem: The shared thesis/practicum choice imposes the thesis-specific immediate-following-semester rule before the route has been selected.
auditCorrections.correction: Attach immediate SSC5302 predecessor/residency rules to actual thesis selections COM5391 or SSC5310. Apply documented last-semester/final-project rules to practicum separately and flag unresolved timing rather than inventing the same prerequisite.

auditCorrections.problem: Pooling all concentration courses into one list is not enough to certify a coherent MBA concentration. Existing review text helps but a guided recommendation must not present any arbitrary three/four courses as a completed concentration.
auditCorrections.correction: Group exact course options by the chosen concentration or label the set as a proposed course collection requiring coordinator confirmation.

auditCorrections.problem: The current seven graduate roadmaps are not the complete AUI graduate catalog. Hiding all other choices can imply nonexistence.
auditCorrections.correction: Use “programs currently supported by the planner” and expose separately sourced exploration targets for MSCSEC, NAMES, MSGDP, MSHRD and MSFinTech, without pretending their roadmaps have been implemented.

auditCorrections.problem: Interest tags and UG-to-master thematic connections are recommendations inferred from curriculum content, not official AUI admission or career-outcome rules.
auditCorrections.correction: Show the matched interest and supporting subject matter in plain language. Keep admissions conditions, approved combined pairings and course-credit waivers separate. Avoid percentage-fit scores or automatic eligibility badges.
